‘Wat vertellen gewone moeders van vandaag hun dochters over de carrousel van cosmetica die vrouwen wordt aangeboden?’ Dat is een vraag waar ik vaak over heb nagedacht wanneer ik zie hoe de meisjes op de kerkbanken opgroeien tot vrouwen. Mijn verwondering is doortrokken van bezorgdheid. Luister met me mee terwijl twee zusters over dit onderwerp praten.

‘Wat doe je met dingen als een beetje concealer tegen acne of zelfs make-up?’ vroeg Minnie aan de zuster die tegenover haar aan tafel zat. ‘Zou je je meisjes toestaan die te gebruiken?’

Dit was niet bepaald een gewoon gespreksonderwerp bij de thee. Krista voelde zich gespannen en vroeg zich af waar Minnie met deze vraag naartoe wilde. ‘Wat bedoel je?’ antwoordde ze. ‘Make-up… wat bedoel je daarmee? Ik denk dat ik dat niet als mogelijkheid voor onze meisjes heb overwogen. Iets om acne te verbergen lijkt me nu weer iets anders. Dat heb ik zelf ook gebruikt, en ik ben nota bene moeder!’

Minnie lachte samen met Krista om haar verlegen bekentenis en legde daarna uit wat ze bedoelde. ‘Toen ik jong was, had ik geen behoefte aan parfum, sieraden of zelfs make-up. Maar nu… mijn meisjes blijven naar allerlei dingen vragen, en ik weet niet goed wat ik hun moet zeggen. Onlangs kwam de vraag op over Ava en haar worsteling met haar bleke teint. Mijn oudste dochter zei: “Weet je, mam, als degenen onder ons met een donkere teint onze wenkbrauwen epileren zodat ze minder opvallen, is het dan zoveel erger als Ava ze donkerder maakt? Weet je, gewoon om haar gezicht wat meer karakter te geven. Of misschien alleen een beetje kleur op haar wangen. Sommigen van ons gebruiken concealer tegen acne. Wat is het verschil? Kan dat kwaad?”’

Krista knikte en haalde haar schouders op in één veelzeggende, nietszeggende beweging. ‘Ik kan die redenering begrijpen.’

Minnie haalde haar schouders op en knikte als reactie op precies dezelfde manier als Krista, terwijl ze verder vertelde. ‘Ik begrijp hun punt ook. Ik zei tegen de meisjes dat ik het niet weet; misschien maakt het niet zoveel uit als ik dacht. En bovendien, als ik om me heen kijk naar de andere jonge vrouwen, zie ik hetzelfde. Ik vraag me weleens af of ik veranderd ben, of dat de tijden veranderd zijn, of wat er aan de hand is. Ik kan me niet herinneren dat ik deze dingen in de kerk zag toen ik jonger was.’

Krista knikte opnieuw, dit keer beslist. Maar Minnie had nog meer te zeggen. ‘Het ging net zo toen de meisjes begonnen te vragen of ze bodyspray en parfum mochten gebruiken. Mijn man wilde niet dat ze dat deden, en ik ook niet, maar ik had geen goede reden om hun te zeggen dat ze het niet mochten. Het is moeilijk, want als je de oudste iets toestaat, wordt dat doorgegeven aan de volgende. Ik vind het nog steeds niet fijn, maar ik zeg tegen mezelf dat het waarschijnlijk gewoon mijn karakter is dat ik niet van geuren houd…’ Haar stem bleef onzeker tussen de twee vrouwen hangen; toen wuifde ze het af met een laatste opmerking. ‘Het is niet alsof het gevaarlijk is of zo.’

Krista knikte opnieuw, verlangend om van onderwerp te veranderen. Ze had geen antwoorden, en Minnies conclusie was eenvoudig genoeg: de dingen die jonge vrouwen de laatste tijd gebruikten, waren niet echt gevaarlijk. Of toch wel?

De ochtend nadat ik hierover had gehoord, hield dit voorval me bezig toen mijn kleine zoon net iets te uitbundig juichte. Zijn stem trok mijn aandacht naar de keuken, waar hij op een gammel stoeltje zat te wiebelen. Hij zwaaide met een gekarteld mes in de lucht, vol kruimels van de appeltaart, en kirde over zijn overwinning: hij had zoiets te pakken gekregen. Mijn ontzetting probeerde me uit mijn stoel te krijgen, maar ik legde een hand op mijn bezorgdheid om die in bedwang te houden. Hij was immers zo blij. Ik was net gaan zitten, voor het eerst die ochtend leek het wel, en ik had nauwelijks de energie voor nog een strijd — zelfs niet voor een strijd met een baby om een mes. Het voelde alsof ik de hele ochtend al strijd voerde, misschien zelfs mijn hele moederschap lang.

Het was toch niet zo gevaarlijk. Hij zou het zo wel neerleggen en iets anders gaan doen. Hoe groot was de kans dat hij echt zou vallen en zich bezeren? En duidelijk genoot hij ervan te ontdekken dat hij dingen kon pakken die hem tot dan toe verboden waren. Het was fijn om hem blij te zien. (Wat is het toch in ons moederhart dat onweerstaanbaar, soms onredelijk, reageert op de aanblik van blije kinderen?)

Zijn ogen glinsterden van triomf terwijl hij het mes boven de taartvorm hield en zijn buik tegen de tafelrand drukte om nog een paar o zo heerlijke kruimels te bemachtigen. Het stoeltje begon onder zijn mollige beentjes vandaan te schuiven. Moest ik dit moment aangrijpen om hem weer iets te leren, of erop vertrouwen dat hij zich niet zou bezeren?

De gedachte aan de gekartelde rand en zijn onwetende roze tong gaf de doorslag. In deze grote wereld zijn er gevaren die hij zich niet kan voorstellen, redenen voor de grenzen die om hem heen zijn gesteld die hij niet begrijpt. Maar zijn moeder weet het wel. Ik begrijp waar messen voor dienen. Het zijn gereedschappen, en ze zijn niet voor kinderen.

Dit is een oproep aan ons moeders. Dit is een dringend verzoek aan vrouwen om de gevaren van deze valstrikken te erkennen. Dit is gericht aan degenen die hebben geproefd van de zoete, kruimelige rand van de gereedschappen die deze wereld voor vrouwen biedt. Dit is gericht aan degenen onder ons met dochters.

Wat leren we hun? Wat zeggen we tegen hen wanneer ze om dat eerste flesje bodyspray vragen? Hoe reageren we wanneer ze voor de derde of driehonderdste keer verschijnen met hun haar keurig in een model dat volgens ons niet de goedkeuring van onze man wegdraagt? Wat doen we als ze een strak, kort vestje van het rek trekken en zeggen: ‘Ach mam, je bent gewoon ouderwets…’?

De bodyspray wordt parfum, en de parfum wordt steeds nadrukkelijker, tot die schaamteloos namen draagt waarvoor een getrouwde vrouw zich zou moeten schamen, laat staan dat een jong meisje ze zou moeten hebben. De kapsels komen en gaan met de trends: hier een beetje hangend, daar een beetje gekruld en — God verhoede het — af en toe glinsterend met highlights. De vestjes worden strakker en de mouwen korter, tot je nauwelijks nog kunt zien dat er onder de lagen gebreide truitjes een eenvoudige jurk zit.

En jij zegt: misschien is het niet zo gevaarlijk als ik dacht. Wat is dit? Is het de berustende zucht van een moeder die haar principes niet aan haar tienerdochters kan overbrengen? Misschien vind jij het, net als ik, ook moeilijk om tijd te maken voor de jongste van het gezin. Het mes in zijn hand maakt hem immers blij. En dat is verfrissend na een ochtend vol driftbuien. Bovendien weet je hoe lekker taartkruimels zijn. Het is niet alsof het echt gevaarlijk is of zo.

Misschien prikt hij zijn tong erdoorheen of steekt hij zijn oog uit, maar verder zijn de risico’s klein.

De Bijbel zegt: …het is beter voor u met één oog het koninkrijk van God binnen te gaan dan met twee ogen in het helse vuur geworpen te worden – Mar 9:47. Dit is een harde boodschap. (Ons is geen gemakkelijke boodschap beloofd.) Maar het begin van het vers biedt een duidelijke, maar vaak over het hoofd geziene uitweg: als iets je tot zonde brengt of ergernis geeft, werp het dan ver van je weg.

De context van dat vers is Jezus’ woorden over het tot struikelen brengen van de kleinen. Vallen je dochters buiten die categorie? Heb je hun geleerd de wereldse verlokkingen weg te werpen die op den duur hun eeuwige ziel zullen schaden? Het woord ‘ergernis’ lees je gemakkelijk over het hoofd, maar het draagt een zware betekenis. Eerder in het hoofdstuk verwijst Jezus ernaar met woorden als ‘molensteen’ en ‘wee’.

Ik stel dat wij moeders medeverantwoordelijk zijn voor dit tot struikelen brengen doordat we onze kleinen — onze meisjes — niet leren wat ware vrouwelijke versiering is. Maar laat het [de versiering] de verborgen mens des harten zijn, in het onverderfelijke sieraad van een zachtmoedige en stille geest, die kostelijk is voor God. Want alzo versierden zich eertijds ook de heilige vrouwen, die op God hoopten… – 1 Petr 3:4-5. Dat woord over de molensteen is op ieder van ons van toepassing. Jezus zegt: …wee dien mens, door welken de ergernis komt! – Mat 18:7. In de Schrift benadrukt Hij deze uitspraak met een ongebruikelijk uitroepteken.

Als de moeders en vrouwen die er ooit voor kozen zich te onthouden van gewoonten die bij wereldse vrouwen horen, niet genoeg reden hebben om hun dochters hetzelfde te laten doen, is de hoop op toekomstige bescheidenheid in onze kerken vervlogen. Vandaag flakkeren de kooltjes onzeker op terwijl de andere kolen uitdoven. De eenvoudige kerken als geheel glijden op verschrikkelijke wijze af naar onbescheidenheid, zowel vanbinnen als vanbuiten. Wie is wijs en verstandig onder u? Die bewijze uit zijn goeden wandel zijn werken in zachtmoedige wijsheid – Jak 3:13.

De opsmuk van de wereldse vrouw is gereedschap van de vijand en is niet bestemd voor de kinderen van God.

Dit is een dringend verzoek, een oproep aan ons moeders om op te staan. Zijn we dapper en vastberaden genoeg om de jongere vrouwen te leren over de gekartelde gevaren van deze wellustige wereld?

Overal om ons heen in de kerk zien we moeders die een pauze hebben ingelast. Moeders die rustig zitten te wiegen, blij dat hun kinderen blij zijn. Hun overtuiging en strijd voor de waarheid zijn ergens tussen het eerste en het laatste kind verdampt. Onze kinderen zullen voor deze overtreding de prijs betalen.

Onze meisjes hebben antwoorden nodig. Jonge vrouwen hebben doelbewuste begeleiding nodig. Pasgetrouwden moeten terechtgewezen worden wanneer ze van het rechte pad beginnen af te raken. De neerwaartse spiraal van afbrokkelende normen staat op het punt met volle kracht verder te draaien nu jonge getrouwde zusters een nieuwe generatie dochters gaan opvoeden met Pinterest en pedicures. Hopen dat ze geen pijn zullen lijden, is niet genoeg.

De beginselen van een heilig leven voor een christelijke vrouw zijn niet veranderd. Ook de zonde die de wereld aandrijft, is niet veranderd. Wat is er dan veranderd? Wij zusters zijn uit het oog verloren welk duidelijke verschil God zegt dat er moet bestaan tussen de vrouwen van God en de vrouwen van deze wereld.

Laten we ter wille van onze Heer Jezus Christus pal staan en een lerares van het goede zijn. In welke levensfase we ook zijn, er komt altijd een jongere vrouw na ons. Laten we hun leren …dat wij, de goddeloosheid en de wereldse begeerlijkheden verzakende, matig en rechtvaardig en godzalig leven zouden in deze tegenwoordige wereld – Tit 2:12.

Nearly 43 years ago, on a warm August afternoon, two 19-year-olds (a young woman and her fiancé) excitedly came out of her parents’ home and walked slowly down a small hill toward a group of 200 waiting people. Her father, a minister, awaited them at the front of the aisle. Flushed with excitement they stood before him and listened to the short message he had prepared concerning marriage. Their hearts beating with anticipation they joyfully answered, “I do,” making a covenant with each other and with God.

They both understood what it meant to remain faithful “through sickness and health, poverty and wealth, for better or worse, till death do us part.” Generations before had shown them that it was possible. Parents and siblings had shown them. Uncles and aunts had shown them. This was going to be bliss into life’s sunset… Or so they thought.

It never entered their minds that great trials would test the very core of their belief and commitment. They went through hard financial times. (The balance in the checkbook was less than the bills that were due.) They went through times of life-changing decisions. (He wanted to quit his job working for his father-in-law building cabinets, receiving a regular paycheck, and begin farming with his father, which didn’t guarantee any income each week, let alone each year. She wasn’t so sure.) They had four children by this time and knew the challenge of crying babies and sleepless nights, which left everyone exhausted. They knew the differences that came up from time to time in church meetings that left them wondering which way they should think. (One brother thought one way and another thought differently, yet this couple respected both brothers.) Twelve years of experiences were behind them; still, married life was blissful and happy. Life’s sun was shining brightly!

Then it happened… The clouds began to roll in thick, angry waves! Eight years of misery and dysfunction were ahead. The devil was hard at work to destroy the unity and joy of these two whose marriage was going so beautifully. He allowed his heart and eyes to look at the allurements of the world and the deception of Satan. Her strong opinions and domineering attitude only added to the problem. Sparing the details, they lost the bliss they once enjoyed. It was a miserable existence for both of them. He was neither repentant nor asking forgiveness, but she continually forgave and pointed the children (five by now) to “we hate the sin, but we love our daddy.” After many years of broken oneness, her commitment to “whither thou goest, I will go” began a miracle. God’s grace was sufficient.

Why are they so happy now?

First, it must be said, it was the power of God working in both of their lives. God didn’t give up on them. He said He wouldn’t; and He didn’t. They were tempted but they didn’t go where Satan wanted them to go. They both have experienced the power of the Holy Spirit to bring them to depths of spiritual communion that they never knew before. It took many heart-wrenching prayers for strength and forgiveness. It took many deep, heartfelt tears of repentance and close accountability to each other. Many and much!

Secondly, as they look back to that time in their lives, there were four principles of God’s Word that were engrained so deeply into their minds that they couldn’t deny them:

  1. A covenant with God is powerful and cannot be broken.
  2. Unconditional love for another person is powerful.
  3. Real and ongoing personal repentance is powerful.
  4. Living a life (moment by moment) of forgiveness is powerful.

When those four God-ordained choices enter a war between the will of God and the wiles of the enemy, the enemy is powerless.

A covenant with God is undeniably unbreakable. When “the books are opened” the covenant will not have changed.

Unconditional love means loving even when it’s not so easy. Fires have a tendency to go out when they have cold water thrown on them. It requires a lot of staying really close to Jesus! Ann’s prayer and plea to God was “Lord, please draw Mark back to You by the power of Your Holy Spirit.” God answered!

When I, Mark, realized what I was losing, both in eternity and in this life with my family, and the depth and sinfulness of my sin, I trembled before God. He brought me to repentance. God began a healing that was exceeding and abundantly above all that Ann and I had ever thought or asked. My deep, heart-wrenching, grief-stricken repentance was real and obvious to her and the family. I took 100% of the blame. Everyone knows “there are always two sides to the story,” yet as the one who had committed the sin, I took full responsibility for my sin and the chaos that was brought into the marriage. I never blamed her for my sin. Humility is not difficult when it is heartfelt and Holy Spirit-guided!

My, Ann’s response to Mark’s repentance was full and free forgiveness. His ongoing expression of repentance and the fact that he took all the blame was powerful in rebuilding trust. It was clear that God was blessing our marriage again! The sun was shining through clouds that were rapidly receding!

Today, 23 years later, photos of that season in our lives or some reminiscent moment is apt to wash up fresh tears of grief and repentance for the pain and wasted years. Ongoing repentance and ready forgiveness have proven beautiful in building trust and a relationship that is sweeter and stronger than ever before! God truly has fulfilled His promise to … restore to [us] the years that the locust hath eaten! (Joel 2:25a) Praise the Lord!

Vor fast 43 Jahren kamen an einem warmen Augustnachmittag zwei 19-Jährige (eine junge Frau und ihr Verlobter) aufgeregt aus dem Haus ihrer Eltern und gingen langsam einen kleinen Hügel hinunter auf eine Gruppe von 200 wartenden Menschen zu. Ihr Vater, ein Prediger, erwartete sie vorne am Mittelgang. Aufgeregt standen sie vor ihm und hörten der kurzen Ansprache zu, die er zur Ehe vorbereitet hatte. Ihre Herzen schlugen erwartungsvoll, als sie freudig „Ja, ich will“ antworteten und miteinander und mit Gott einen Bund schlossen.

Beiden war klar, was es bedeutete, einander treu zu bleiben „in Krankheit und Gesundheit, in Armut und Wohlstand, in guten wie in schlechten Zeiten, bis dass der Tod uns scheidet“. Frühere Generationen hatten ihnen gezeigt, dass es möglich war. Ihre Eltern und Geschwister hatten es ihnen gezeigt. Ihre Onkel und Tanten hatten es ihnen gezeigt. Ihr Leben sollte bis in den Abend hinein voller Glück sein … Dachten sie zumindest.

Nie wäre ihnen in den Sinn gekommen, dass schwere Prüfungen den Kern ihres Glaubens und ihrer Hingabe auf die Probe stellen würden. Sie machten schwierige Zeiten mit knappen Finanzen durch. (Der Kontostand war niedriger als die fälligen Rechnungen.) Sie mussten lebensverändernde Entscheidungen treffen. (Er wollte seine Stelle bei seinem Schwiegervater aufgeben, wo er Schränke baute und ein regelmäßiges Gehalt bekam, und mit seinem Vater in die Landwirtschaft einsteigen, was weder wöchentlich noch gar jährlich ein Einkommen garantierte. Sie war sich nicht so sicher.) Inzwischen hatten sie vier Kinder und kannten die Herausforderung schreiender Babys und schlafloser Nächte, die alle erschöpft zurückließen. Sie kannten die Meinungsverschiedenheiten, die von Zeit zu Zeit in Gemeindeversammlungen aufkamen und sie fragend zurückließen, was sie denken sollten. (Ein Bruder dachte so, ein anderer anders, doch das Paar achtete beide Brüder.) Zwölf Jahre voller Erlebnisse lagen hinter ihnen; dennoch war das Eheleben voller Glück und Freude. Die Sonne des Lebens schien hell!

Dann geschah es … Dichte, düstere Wolken zogen in wütenden Wellen auf! Acht Jahre voller Elend und Zerrüttung lagen vor ihnen. Der Teufel setzte alles daran, die Einheit und Freude dieser beiden zu zerstören, deren Ehe so wunderbar verlief. Er ließ zu, dass sein Herz und seine Augen sich von den Verlockungen der Welt und der Täuschung Satans hinreißen ließen. Ihre starken Meinungen und ihre herrische Haltung verschlimmerten das Problem nur noch. Um die Einzelheiten kurz zu halten: Sie verloren das Glück, das sie einst gekannt hatten. Für beide war es ein elendes Leben. Er bereute nicht und bat auch nicht um Vergebung, doch sie vergab ihm immer wieder und wies die Kinder (inzwischen waren es fünf) darauf hin: „Wir hassen die Sünde, aber wir lieben unseren Papa.“ Nach vielen Jahren zerbrochener Verbundenheit setzte ihr Entschluss, „wohin du gehst, dahin gehe auch ich“, ein Wunder in Gang. Gottes Gnade war genug.

Warum sind sie jetzt so glücklich?

Zunächst muss gesagt werden: Es war die Kraft Gottes, die im Leben beider wirkte. Gott gab sie nicht auf. Er hatte gesagt, dass er es nicht tun würde, und das tat er auch nicht. Sie wurden versucht, gingen aber nicht den Weg, den Satan für sie wollte. Beide haben die Kraft des Heiligen Geistes erlebt, die sie zu einer Tiefe geistlicher Gemeinschaft führte, wie sie sie zuvor nie gekannt hatten. Es brauchte viele herzzerreißende Gebete um Kraft und Vergebung. Es brauchte viele tiefe, von Herzen kommende Tränen der Reue und gegenseitige Rechenschaft. Vieles und sehr viel!

Zweitens gab es, als sie auf diese Zeit ihres Lebens zurückblickten, vier Grundsätze aus Gottes Wort, die sich so tief in ihren Herzen eingeprägt hatten, dass sie sie nicht leugnen konnten:

  1. Ein Bund mit Gott ist mächtig und kann nicht gebrochen werden.
  2. Bedingungslose Liebe zu einem anderen Menschen ist mächtig.
  3. Echte und anhaltende persönliche Umkehr ist mächtig.
  4. Ein Leben zu führen, in dem man Augenblick für Augenblick vergibt, ist mächtig.

Wenn diese vier von Gott bestimmten Entscheidungen in einen Kampf zwischen Gottes Willen und den Ränken des Feindes eintreten, ist der Feind machtlos.

Ein Bund mit Gott ist unbestreitbar unauflöslich. Wenn „die Bücher geöffnet werden“, wird sich an dem Bund nichts geändert haben.

Bedingungslose Liebe bedeutet, auch dann zu lieben, wenn es nicht so leicht ist. Feuer neigen dazu zu erlöschen, wenn man kaltes Wasser darüber schüttet. Es erfordert, Jesus wirklich ganz nahe zu bleiben! Anns Gebet und Bitte an Gott lautete: „Herr, bitte zieh Mark durch die Kraft deines Heiligen Geistes zu dir zurück.“ Gott erhörte ihr Gebet!

Als ich, Mark, erkannte, was ich verlor – sowohl für die Ewigkeit als auch in diesem Leben mit meiner Familie – und wie tief und sündhaft meine Sünde war, zitterte ich vor Gott. Er führte mich zur Umkehr. Gott begann einen Heilungsprozess, der weit über alles hinausging, was Ann und ich je gedacht oder erbeten hatten. Meine tiefe, herzzerreißende, von Kummer erfüllte Umkehr war für sie und die Familie echt und offensichtlich. Ich übernahm zu 100 % die Schuld. Jeder weiß: „Zu einer Geschichte gehören immer zwei Seiten“, doch als derjenige, der die Sünde begangen hatte, übernahm ich die volle Verantwortung für meine Sünde und das Chaos, das in die Ehe gekommen war. Ich gab ihr niemals die Schuld an meiner Sünde. Demut fällt nicht schwer, wenn sie von Herzen kommt und vom Heiligen Geist geleitet wird!

Meine – Anns – Antwort auf Marks Umkehr war uneingeschränkte und unbedingte Vergebung. Dass er fortwährend Umkehr zeigte und die ganze Schuld auf sich nahm, trug entscheidend dazu bei, das Vertrauen wieder aufzubauen. Es war deutlich, dass Gott unsere Ehe wieder segnete! Durch die rasch zurückweichenden Wolken schien die Sonne!

Heute, 23 Jahre später, lassen Fotos aus jener Zeit unseres Lebens oder manche Erinnerung daran oft aufs Neue Tränen des Kummers und der Reue über den Schmerz und die verlorenen Jahre aufsteigen. Anhaltende Umkehr und bereitwillige Vergebung haben sich als etwas Wunderschönes erwiesen: Sie haben Vertrauen und eine Beziehung wachsen lassen, die süßer und stärker ist als je zuvor! Gott hat sein Versprechen wirklich erfüllt, … [uns] die Jahre zu erstatten, welche die Heuschrecke gefressen hat! (Joel 2:25a) Lob sei dem Herrn!

“What are plain mothers of today telling their daughters about the carousel of cosmetics proffered for women?” This is a question I have pondered many times as I observe the girls in the church benches grow into womanhood. My wonder is weighted with concern. Listen in with me as two sisters talk about this topic.

“What do you do about things like a touch of acne cover-up or even make-up?” Minnie asked the sister sitting across the table from her. “Would you let your girls use them?”

This wasn’t exactly a normal tea-time topic. Krista tightened inside, wondering where Minnie might be going with this question. “What do you mean?” she replied. “Make-up…what do you mean by that? I guess that’s not something I’ve considered as an option for our girls. Now something to cover acne seems different to me. I’ve used that myself, and I’m a mom!”

Minnie chuckled with Krista over her sheepish confession before explaining herself. “When I was a young woman, I didn’t struggle with wanting to wear perfume or jewelry or even make-up. But now…my girls keep asking about things, and I’m not sure what to tell them. Recently a question came up about Ava and her struggle with her pale complexion. My oldest daughter said, ‘You know, Mom, if those of us with dark complexions pluck our eyebrows so they don’t stand out as much, is it any worse if Ava darkens hers? You know, just to add a little character to her face. Or maybe just a dab of color on her cheeks. Some of us wear acne cover up. What’s the difference? Is there any harm in that?’”

Krista nodded and shrugged in one expressive, noncommittal movement. “I can understand that reasoning.”

Minnie’s responsive shrug and nod looked a lot like Krista’s as she continued with her story. “I can see their point, too. I told the girls I don’t know; maybe it doesn’t matter as much as I thought it did. And besides, when I look around at the rest of our young women, I see the same things. I kind of wonder if I’ve changed, or if the times have changed, or what. I don’t remember seeing these things in the church when I was younger.”

Krista nodded again, this time with certainty. But Minnie had more to say. “It was the same way when the girls wanted to start wearing body sprays and perfumes. My husband didn’t want them to, and neither did I, but I didn’t have a good reason to tell them not to. It’s hard because when you let the oldest one do one thing, it gets passed on down the line. I still don’t like it, but I tell myself it’s probably just my personality to not like scents…” Her voice hung uncertainly between the two women, then she shrugged off a closing comment. “It’s not like it’s dangerous or anything.”

Krista nodded again, anxious to get the subject changed. She didn’t have answers, and Minnie’s conclusion was simple enough: these things young women were using lately weren’t really dangerous. Or were they?

This incident was occupying my mind the morning after I heard about it when my small son crowed just a little too happily. His tone tugged my attention into the kitchen where he rocked on a rickety chair. He waved a serrated knife in the air, laden with apple cake crumbs, burbling about his victory in reaching such an item. My dismay tried to stir me from my chair, but I laid a staying hand over my concern. He was so happy, after all. I had just sat down for what felt like the first time in the morning and I hardly had the energy for another battle—even just a battle with a baby over a knife. I felt like I had been waging battles all morning, maybe all my motherhood.

It wasn’t that dangerous, surely. He’d lay it down in a moment and go on to do something else. What were the odds he would actually fall and get hurt? And he was plainly pleased to experiment with his ability to reach things hitherto forbidden. It felt good to see him happy. (What is it in our mother-hearts that irresistibly, sometimes unreasonably, responds to seeing our children happy?)

His eyes glittered with triumph as he held the knife over the cake pan, pushing his tummy against the table edge in order to get a few more oh-so-sweet crumbs. The chair began scooting out from under his fat little legs. Should I take the moment to teach another lesson or should I take the chance he wouldn’t get hurt?

The thought of the serrated edge and his ignorant pink tongue won out. There are dangers in this big world he can’t imagine, reasons for the boundaries set around him he doesn’t comprehend. But his mother knows. I understand what knives are for. They are tools and they are not for children.

This is a call for us mothers. This is a plea for ladies to recognize the dangers of these entrapments. This is for ones who have tasted the sweet, crumby edge of this world’s tools for women. This is for those of us with daughters.

What are we teaching them? What are we saying to them when they beg for that first bottle of body spray? What is our response when they appear for the third or three-hundredth time with their hair nattily arranged in a style we know our husbands do not approve of? What do we do when they pull a snug little shrug from the sweater rack and say, “Aw, Mom, you’re just outdated…”?

The body spray turns into perfume, and the perfume gets louder until it brazenly wears titles a married woman should blush to see, let alone a young girl possess. The hairstyles ebb and flow with the trends, drooping here a little, curling there a little, and—God forbid—occasionally glinting with highlights. The shrugs get tighter, and the sleeves get shorter until it becomes hard to see there is a plain dress under the layers of pullover knits.

And you respond, maybe it’s not as dangerous as I thought it was. What is this? Is it the surrendering sigh of a mother unable to pass her principles on to her teenage daughters? Perhaps, like me, you also find it challenging to take time for the baby of the family. The knife in his hand, after all, makes him happy. And that is refreshing after a morning of tantrums. Besides, you know how yummy cake crumbs are. It’s not like it’s really dangerous or anything.

He might pierce his tongue or stab out his eye, but otherwise, the risks are low.

The Bible says …it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire –Mar 9:47. This is a hard gospel. (We weren’t promised an easy one.) But the beginning of the verse offers an obvious yet often overlooked escape route—if something causes you to offend, or be offended, cast it far from you.

The context of that verse is Jesus’ words on offending the little ones. Do your daughters fall outside that label? Have you taught them to cast away the worldly enticements that, long term, will offend their eternal souls? The word offend is easy to read over, yet it is piled with portent. Earlier in the chapter, Jesus references it with words like “millstone” and “woe.”

I am proposing that we mothers are responsible in this offending by failing to teach our little ones—our girls—about true womanly adornment. But let it [the adornment] be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves… –1Pe 3:4-5. That millstone word applies to each of us. Jesus says, …woe to that [wo]man by whom the offence cometh! –Mat 18:7. He emphasizes this statement in Scripture with an uncharacteristic exclamation point.

If the mothers and women who once chose to abstain from habits which belong to women of the world don’t have enough reason for their daughters to do the same, hope is extinguished for the future modesty of our churches. Today, the embers flicker uncertainly as fellow coals grow cold. The plain churches as a whole are on a terrible slide of immodesty, both inside and out. Who is a wise [wo]man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom –Jas 3:13.

The worldly woman’s trappings are tools of the enemy and they are not for the children of God.

This is a plea, a call, for us mothers to stand up. Are we brave enough, committed enough, to teach the younger women the serrated dangers of this lustful world?

All around us in the church is the evidence of mothers who are on break. Mothers rocking serenely, happy to see their children happy. Their conviction and fight for truth evaporated somewhere between the first and last child. Our children will pay for this offense.

Our girls need answers. Young women need intentional guidance. Newlyweds need rebuke when they start getting off track. The downward spiral of decaying standards is about to spin with a vengeance as young-married sisters begin to raise a new generation of daughters on Pinterest and pedicures. Hoping they won’t get hurt is not going to cut it.

The principles of holy living for a Christian woman have not changed. Neither has the sin that motivates the world. What, then, has changed? We as sisters have lost sight of the clear difference that God says should exist between the women of God and the women of this world.

For the cause of our Lord Jesus Christ, let’s take a stand and be a teacher of good things. Whatever our stage in life, there is a younger woman coming behind us. Let us teach them …that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world –Tit 2:12.

“如今，普通的母亲会怎样告诉女儿，面对摆在女性面前、令人眼花缭乱的化妆品？”每当我看着教会长椅上的女孩们长大成人时，心里总会反复思量这个问题。我对此忧心忡忡。请和我一起听两位姐妹谈谈这个话题。

“像稍微遮一下痘痘，甚至化妆这类事情，你怎么看？”明妮问坐在桌子对面的姐妹，“你会让你的女儿用吗？”

这可不是什么寻常的茶叙话题。克丽丝塔心里一紧，猜想着明妮问这个问题究竟想说什么。“你是什么意思？”她回答，“化妆……你说的是什么意思？我想，我从没考虑过让女儿们用这个。不过，遮一下痘痘在我看来又是另一回事。我自己就用过，而且我还是个妈妈呢！”

明妮和克丽丝塔一起为她这番有些不好意思的坦白笑了笑，接着解释道：“我年轻时，并不为自己想用香水、首饰，甚至化妆品而烦恼。可是现在……我的女儿们总在问这问那，我不知道该怎么回答她们。最近，她们问起了艾娃和她对自己肤色苍白这件事的烦恼。我的大女儿说：‘你知道，妈妈，我们这些肤色较深的人会拔眉毛，让眉毛不那么显眼；那艾娃把眉毛画深一点，又有什么不好呢？只是让她的脸看起来多一点神采。或者只在脸颊上稍微涂点颜色。我们有些人会用遮瑕膏遮痘痘。有什么区别呢？这样有什么害处吗？’”

克丽丝塔点点头，又耸了耸肩，这一个动作既表达了她的理解，也没有明确表态。“我能理解这种想法。”

明妮回应时耸肩点头的样子和克丽丝塔很像，她接着讲道：“我也能理解她们的道理。我告诉女儿们，我不知道；也许这件事不像我原先想的那么要紧。而且，我看看周围其他年轻姐妹，也都能看到同样的事情。我不禁想，是我变了，还是时代变了，或者究竟是怎么回事。我年轻时，不记得教会里有这些东西。”

克丽丝塔又点了点头，这次态度很肯定。但明妮还有话要说：“女儿们想开始用身体喷雾和香水时，情况也一样。我丈夫不愿她们用，我也不愿意，可我又没有充分的理由告诉她们不可以。难就难在，你让大女儿做了一件事，后面的女儿也会跟着做。我到现在还是不喜欢这些东西，可我总对自己说，我大概只是天生不喜欢香味……”她的话音悬在两人之间，透着犹疑。随后，她耸耸肩，像是要结束这个话题：“这又不是什么危险的东西。”

克丽丝塔又点了点头，急着想换个话题。她没有答案，而明妮的结论简单明了：年轻女子近来用的这些东西其实并不危险。真的是这样吗？

第二天早晨，我听说这件事后，心里一直想着它。就在那时，小儿子兴高采烈地咿呀叫了一声，声音稍稍有些得意。他的语气把我的注意力引到了厨房，只见他坐在一把摇摇晃晃的椅子上。他挥舞着一把锯齿刀，刀上沾满了苹果蛋糕屑，还咿咿呀呀地炫耀自己竟能拿到这样的东西。我心里一惊，想从椅子上站起来，可还是把一只手按在忧虑上，强迫自己坐着不动。毕竟，他那么开心。我刚坐下，感觉这大概是整个早上第一次坐下来，实在没什么力气再打一场仗——哪怕只是为了把刀从小宝宝手里拿走。我觉得自己整个早上都在打仗，也许整个为人母的日子都是如此。

这肯定没那么危险。他一会儿就会把刀放下，去做别的事。真摔倒受伤的可能性有多大呢？而且，他显然很高兴能试试自己伸手拿到以前不许碰的东西。看到他开心，我心里也觉得好受。（做母亲的心里究竟有什么，竟会在看到孩子开心时无法抗拒地——有时甚至不合情理地——受到触动？）

他把刀举在蛋糕盘上方，眼睛因胜利而闪闪发亮，肚子抵着桌沿，只为再够到几粒甜得不得了的蛋糕屑。椅子开始从他胖乎乎的小腿下往外滑。我该趁此机会再教他一课，还是该赌一把，盼着他不会受伤？

一想到锯齿刀刃和他毫无戒心的粉红小舌头，我最终还是决定阻止他。在这个广阔的世界里，有许多危险是他想象不到的；围绕他设下的种种界限，也有他不明白的缘由。但他的母亲知道。我明白刀子是做什么用的。它们是工具，不是给孩子玩的。

这是对我们做母亲的呼吁。这是恳请姐妹们认清这些诱惑陷阱的危险。这是写给那些尝过世上为女性预备的工具那甜蜜而诱人的滋味的人。这是写给我们这些有女儿的人。

我们在教她们什么？她们央求要第一瓶身体喷雾时，我们对她们说了什么？她们第三次、或第三百次梳着我们知道丈夫不赞成的时髦发型出现在我们面前时，我们怎么回应？她们从毛衣架上拿起一件贴身的小披肩，说：“哎呀，妈妈，你就是过时了……”时，我们又怎么办？

身体喷雾变成了香水，香水的气味越来越浓，最后竟堂而皇之地带上已婚妇女都该羞于见到的香型名称，更别说年轻女孩拥有它们了。发型随着潮流起伏变化，这里垂下一点，那里卷起一点——但愿别这样——偶尔还闪现几缕挑染。小披肩越来越紧，袖子越来越短，直到针织套衫一层层叠穿在外面，让人几乎看不出里面还有一条朴素的连衣裙。

而你却回应说，也许事情并不像我以为的那么危险。这是怎么回事？这是母亲无力把自己的原则传给青春期女儿时，发出的妥协叹息吗？或许你也和我一样，发现自己很难抽出时间管教家里的小宝宝。毕竟，刀在他手里，他很开心。而在一个充满哭闹的早晨之后，这份开心也让人觉得轻松。况且，你知道蛋糕屑有多好吃。这又不是什么真正危险的东西。

他可能会刺穿舌头，或把眼睛戳瞎；除此之外，风险不大。

圣经说：……你只有一只眼进入神的国，强如有两只眼被丢进地狱的火里——可9:47。这是严厉的福音。（我们并没有被应许会有轻松的福音。）但这节经文的开头给出了一个明显却常被忽略的脱身之道——如果有什么事使你犯罪，或使人跌倒，就把它远远丢开。

这节经文的上下文，是耶稣谈论使小子跌倒。你的女儿们不在这些“小子”之列吗？你教过她们弃绝那些属世的诱惑吗？这些诱惑长远而言会使她们永恒的灵魂跌倒。“跌倒”这个词很容易被一眼略过，却蕴含着重大的警告。在本章较前面，耶稣用“磨石”和“有祸了”之类的话提到这件事。

我认为，我们做母亲的若没有教导自己的小孩子——我们的女儿——什么才是真正的女性装饰，就要为使她们跌倒负责任。只要以里面存着长久温柔、安静的心为妆饰；这在神面前是极宝贵的。因为古时仰赖神的圣洁妇人，正是以此为妆饰……——彼前3:4-5。磨石这个警告适用于我们每一个人。耶稣说：……那叫人跌倒的有祸了！——太18:7。祂在圣经中用一个不寻常的感叹号来强调这句话。

如果那些曾经选择不沾染世俗女子习惯的母亲和妇女，拿不出足够理由让女儿也这样做，那么我们教会将来在端庄方面就没有希望了。如今，余烬摇曳不定，身边的炭火也渐渐冷却。整体而言，朴素派教会正在端庄方面走上一条可怕的下坡路，无论内在还是外在都是如此。你们中间谁是有智慧、有见识的呢？他就当以智慧的温柔显出他的善行来——雅3:13。

世俗女子的装饰是仇敌的工具，不是神儿女该用的。

这是一次恳求，一声呼吁，呼吁我们做母亲的挺身而出。我们有足够的勇气和决心，教导年轻女子看清这个淫乱世界那如锯齿般锋利的危险吗？

在教会里，随处可见母亲们松懈下来的迹象。她们安然地摇着孩子，看到孩子开心就满足了。她们对真理的信念和争战，不知在第一个孩子和最后一个孩子之间的哪个时候消散了。我们的孩子将为这过犯付出代价。

我们的女孩需要答案。年轻女子需要有意识的引导。新婚夫妇开始走偏时，需要有人责备她们。标准不断败坏、一路下滑的漩涡即将猛烈旋转，因为年轻的已婚姐妹开始在 Pinterest 和美甲护理的熏陶下养育新一代女儿。光盼着她们不会受伤，是行不通的。

基督徒妇女圣洁生活的原则没有改变，推动世界犯罪的罪也没有改变。那么，究竟是什么变了？我们姐妹已经看不清神所说的、神的妇女与世上妇女之间应该存在的鲜明区别。

为了我们的主耶稣基督，让我们站出来，作教导人行善的榜样。无论我们处在人生的哪个阶段，都有比我们年轻的妇女跟在后面。让我们教导她们：……除去不敬虔的心和世俗的情欲，在今世自守、公义、敬虔度日——多2:12。

Nearly 43 years ago, on a warm August afternoon, two 19-year-olds (a young woman and her fiancé) excitedly came out of her parents’ home and walked slowly down a small hill toward a group of 200 waiting people. Her father, a minister, awaited them at the front of the aisle. Flushed with excitement they stood before him and listened to the short message he had prepared concerning marriage. Their hearts beating with anticipation they joyfully answered, “I do,” making a covenant with each other and with God.

They both understood what it meant to remain faithful “through sickness and health, poverty and wealth, for better or worse, till death do us part.” Generations before had shown them that it was possible. Parents and siblings had shown them. Uncles and aunts had shown them. This was going to be bliss into life’s sunset… Or so they thought.

It never entered their minds that great trials would test the very core of their belief and commitment. They went through hard financial times. (The balance in the checkbook was less than the bills that were due.) They went through times of life-changing decisions. (He wanted to quit his job working for his father-in-law building cabinets, receiving a regular paycheck, and begin farming with his father, which didn’t guarantee any income each week, let alone each year. She wasn’t so sure.) They had four children by this time and knew the challenge of crying babies and sleepless nights, which left everyone exhausted. They knew the differences that came up from time to time in church meetings that left them wondering which way they should think. (One brother thought one way and another thought differently, yet this couple respected both brothers.) Twelve years of experiences were behind them; still, married life was blissful and happy. Life’s sun was shining brightly!

Then it happened… The clouds began to roll in thick, angry waves! Eight years of misery and dysfunction were ahead. The devil was hard at work to destroy the unity and joy of these two whose marriage was going so beautifully. He allowed his heart and eyes to look at the allurements of the world and the deception of Satan. Her strong opinions and domineering attitude only added to the problem. Sparing the details, they lost the bliss they once enjoyed. It was a miserable existence for both of them. He was neither repentant nor asking forgiveness, but she continually forgave and pointed the children (five by now) to “we hate the sin, but we love our daddy.” After many years of broken oneness, her commitment to “whither thou goest, I will go” began a miracle. God’s grace was sufficient.

Why are they so happy now?

First, it must be said, it was the power of God working in both of their lives. God didn’t give up on them. He said He wouldn’t; and He didn’t. They were tempted but they didn’t go where Satan wanted them to go. They both have experienced the power of the Holy Spirit to bring them to depths of spiritual communion that they never knew before. It took many heart-wrenching prayers for strength and forgiveness. It took many deep, heartfelt tears of repentance and close accountability to each other. Many and much!

Secondly, as they look back to that time in their lives, there were four principles of God’s Word that were engrained so deeply into their minds that they couldn’t deny them:

  1. A covenant with God is powerful and cannot be broken.
  2. Unconditional love for another person is powerful.
  3. Real and ongoing personal repentance is powerful.
  4. Living a life (moment by moment) of forgiveness is powerful.

When those four God-ordained choices enter a war between the will of God and the wiles of the enemy, the enemy is powerless.

A covenant with God is undeniably unbreakable. When “the books are opened” the covenant will not have changed.

Unconditional love means loving even when it’s not so easy. Fires have a tendency to go out when they have cold water thrown on them. It requires a lot of staying really close to Jesus! Ann’s prayer and plea to God was “Lord, please draw Mark back to You by the power of Your Holy Spirit.” God answered!

When I, Mark, realized what I was losing, both in eternity and in this life with my family, and the depth and sinfulness of my sin, I trembled before God. He brought me to repentance. God began a healing that was exceeding and abundantly above all that Ann and I had ever thought or asked. My deep, heart-wrenching, grief-stricken repentance was real and obvious to her and the family. I took 100% of the blame. Everyone knows “there are always two sides to the story,” yet as the one who had committed the sin, I took full responsibility for my sin and the chaos that was brought into the marriage. I never blamed her for my sin. Humility is not difficult when it is heartfelt and Holy Spirit-guided!

My, Ann’s response to Mark’s repentance was full and free forgiveness. His ongoing expression of repentance and the fact that he took all the blame was powerful in rebuilding trust. It was clear that God was blessing our marriage again! The sun was shining through clouds that were rapidly receding!

Today, 23 years later, photos of that season in our lives or some reminiscent moment is apt to wash up fresh tears of grief and repentance for the pain and wasted years. Ongoing repentance and ready forgiveness have proven beautiful in building trust and a relationship that is sweeter and stronger than ever before! God truly has fulfilled His promise to … restore to [us] the years that the locust hath eaten! (Joel 2:25a) Praise the Lord!

Karibu miaka 43 iliyopita, alasiri moja yenye joto mwezi Agosti, vijana wawili wa miaka 19 (msichana na mchumba wake) walitoka kwa furaha nyumbani kwa wazazi wake na kutembea polepole kushuka kwenye kilima kidogo kuelekea kwenye kikundi cha watu 200 waliokuwa wakingoja. Baba yake, ambaye alikuwa mhudumu wa kanisa, aliwasubiri mbele ya njia ya katikati. Wakiwa wamejawa na msisimko, walisimama mbele yake na kusikiliza ujumbe mfupi aliokuwa ameutayarisha kuhusu ndoa. Mioyo yao ikidunda kwa hamu, walijibu kwa furaha, “Nakubali,” wakifanya agano wao kwa wao na pamoja na Mungu.

Wote wawili walielewa maana ya kubaki waaminifu “katika ugonjwa na afya, umaskini na utajiri, kwa mema au mabaya, mpaka kifo kitakapotutenganisha.” Vizazi vilivyowatangulia vilikuwa vimewaonyesha kwamba hilo liliwezekana. Wazazi na ndugu zao walikuwa wamewaonyesha. Shangazi, wajomba, ami na binamu zao walikuwa wamewaonyesha. Maisha yao yangekuwa ya furaha hadi machweo ya maisha… Au ndivyo walivyofikiri.

Haikuwahi kuwajia akilini kwamba majaribu makubwa yangejaribu kiini hasa cha imani na kujitoa kwao. Walipitia nyakati ngumu za kifedha. (Salio la hundi lilikuwa chini ya kiasi cha bili zilizopaswa kulipwa.) Walipitia nyakati za maamuzi yaliyobadili maisha. (Alitaka kuacha kazi yake ya kutengeneza kabati pamoja na baba mkwe wake, iliyompatia mshahara wa kawaida, na kuanza kulima pamoja na baba yake, jambo ambalo halikuhakikisha mapato ya kila wiki, sembuse ya kila mwaka. Yeye hakuwa na uhakika.) Kufikia wakati huo walikuwa na watoto wanne na walijua changamoto ya watoto wachanga kulia na kukosa usingizi usiku, hali iliyowaacha wote wakiwa wamechoka. Walijua tofauti zilizojitokeza mara kwa mara katika mikutano ya kanisa na kuwaacha wakijiuliza wanapaswa kufikiri nini. (Ndugu mmoja alifikiri hivi na mwingine alifikiri tofauti, lakini wenzi hawa waliwaheshimu ndugu wote wawili.) Miaka kumi na miwili ya mambo waliyopitia ilikuwa imepita; hata hivyo, maisha ya ndoa yalikuwa ya furaha na shangwe. Jua la maisha lilikuwa likiangaza kwa mng’ao!

Kisha likatokea… Mawingu yakaanza kutanda kwa mawimbi mazito na makali! Miaka minane ya taabu na hali isiyofaa ilikuwa mbele yao. Ibilisi alikuwa akifanya kazi kwa bidii ili kuharibu umoja na furaha ya hawa wawili ambao ndoa yao ilikuwa ikienda vizuri sana. Aliruhusu moyo na macho yake kuvutiwa na mambo ya ulimwengu na udanganyifu wa Shetani. Maoni yake yenye msimamo mkali na tabia yake ya kutawala viliongeza tu tatizo. Bila kueleza mengi, walipoteza furaha waliyokuwa wamewahi kufurahia. Maisha yao wote wawili yakawa ya taabu. Yeye hakutubu wala kuomba msamaha, lakini yeye aliendelea kusamehe na kuwaelekeza watoto (watano kufikia wakati huo) kwenye kauli hii: “Tunachukia dhambi, lakini tunampenda baba yetu.” Baada ya miaka mingi ya kutokuwa kitu kimoja, kujitoa kwake kwa kauli “niendako, nitakwenda” kulianza muujiza. Neema ya Mungu ilitosha.

Kwa nini wana furaha sana sasa?

Kwanza, lazima isemwe kwamba ilikuwa nguvu za Mungu zikifanya kazi katika maisha yao wote wawili. Mungu hakuwatelekeza. Alisema hatafanya hivyo; na hakufanya. Walijaribiwa lakini hawakuenda kule ambako Shetani alitaka waende. Wote wawili wameonja nguvu za Roho Mtakatifu zilizowaongoza kwenye kina cha ushirika wa kiroho ambacho hawakukijua hapo awali. Ilihitaji sala nyingi za kuumiza moyo, za kuomba nguvu na msamaha. Ilihitaji machozi mengi ya ndani kabisa, ya dhati ya toba, na kuwajibishana kwa karibu. Mengi sana!

Pili, wanapotazama nyuma wakati huo wa maisha yao, kulikuwa na kanuni nne za Neno la Mungu zilizokuwa zimekita mizizi ndani ya akili zao kiasi kwamba hawangeweza kuzikana:

  1. Agano pamoja na Mungu lina nguvu na haliwezi kuvunjwa.
  2. Upendo usio na masharti kwa mtu mwingine una nguvu.
  3. Toba ya kweli na ya kudumu ya mtu binafsi ina nguvu.
  4. Kuishi maisha (wakati baada ya wakati) ya kusamehe kuna nguvu.

Chaguo hizo nne zilizowekwa na Mungu zinapoingia katika vita kati ya mapenzi ya Mungu na hila za adui, adui hana nguvu.

Agano pamoja na Mungu haliwezi kuvunjwa, bila shaka. “Vitabu vitakapofunguliwa,” agano halitakuwa limebadilika.

Upendo usio na masharti humaanisha kupenda hata wakati si rahisi sana. Moto huwa na tabia ya kuzimika unapomwagiwa maji baridi. Inahitaji kukaa karibu sana na Yesu! Sala na ombi la Ann kwa Mungu lilikuwa, “Bwana, tafadhali mrudishe Mark kwako kwa nguvu za Roho wako Mtakatifu.” Mungu alijibu!

Mimi, Mark, nilipotambua kile nilichokuwa nikipoteza, katika umilele na katika maisha haya pamoja na familia yangu, na jinsi dhambi yangu ilivyokuwa kubwa na ya dhambi, nilitetemeka mbele za Mungu. Aliniongoza kwenye toba. Mungu alianza uponyaji uliopita kiasi na ulio mwingi sana kuliko yote ambayo mimi na Ann tuliwahi kufikiri au kuomba. Toba yangu ya ndani sana, iliyoumia moyoni na kujaa huzuni ilikuwa ya kweli na ilionekana wazi kwake na kwa familia. Nilibeba lawama zote kwa asilimia 100. Kila mtu anajua kwamba “daima kuna pande mbili za hadithi,” lakini mimi, nikiwa ndiye niliyetenda dhambi, nilichukua jukumu kamili kwa dhambi yangu na machafuko yaliyoletwa ndani ya ndoa. Sikuwahi kumlaumu yeye kwa dhambi yangu. Unyenyekevu si mgumu unapokuwa wa dhati na kuongozwa na Roho Mtakatifu!

Mwitikio wangu, Ann, kwa toba ya Mark ulikuwa msamaha kamili na wa bure. Kuendelea kwake kuonyesha toba na ukweli kwamba alibeba lawama zote kulikuwa na nguvu katika kujenga upya tumaini. Ilikuwa wazi kwamba Mungu alikuwa akibariki ndoa yetu tena! Jua lilikuwa likiangaza katikati ya mawingu yaliyokuwa yakitoweka haraka!

Leo, miaka 23 baadaye, picha za kipindi hicho cha maisha yetu au tukio fulani linalotukumbusha wakati huo hutuleta tena machozi mapya ya huzuni na toba kwa maumivu na miaka iliyopotea. Toba inayoendelea na msamaha unaotolewa bila kusita vimethibitika kuwa vyema katika kujenga tumaini na uhusiano ulio mtamu na wenye nguvu zaidi kuliko wakati mwingine wowote! Kwa kweli Mungu ametimiza ahadi yake ya … kuturudishia miaka iliyoliwa na nzige! (Yoeli 2:25a) Bwana asifiwe!

Nearly 43 years ago, on a warm August afternoon, two 19-year-olds (a young woman and her fiancé) excitedly came out of her parents’ home and walked slowly down a small hill toward a group of 200 waiting people. Her father, a minister, awaited them at the front of the aisle. Flushed with excitement they stood before him and listened to the short message he had prepared concerning marriage. Their hearts beating with anticipation they joyfully answered, “I do,” making a covenant with each other and with God.

They both understood what it meant to remain faithful “through sickness and health, poverty and wealth, for better or worse, till death do us part.” Generations before had shown them that it was possible. Parents and siblings had shown them. Uncles and aunts had shown them. This was going to be bliss into life’s sunset… Or so they thought.

It never entered their minds that great trials would test the very core of their belief and commitment. They went through hard financial times. (The balance in the checkbook was less than the bills that were due.) They went through times of life-changing decisions. (He wanted to quit his job working for his father-in-law building cabinets, receiving a regular paycheck, and begin farming with his father, which didn’t guarantee any income each week, let alone each year. She wasn’t so sure.) They had four children by this time and knew the challenge of crying babies and sleepless nights, which left everyone exhausted. They knew the differences that came up from time to time in church meetings that left them wondering which way they should think. (One brother thought one way and another thought differently, yet this couple respected both brothers.) Twelve years of experiences were behind them; still, married life was blissful and happy. Life’s sun was shining brightly!

Then it happened… The clouds began to roll in thick, angry waves! Eight years of misery and dysfunction were ahead. The devil was hard at work to destroy the unity and joy of these two whose marriage was going so beautifully. He allowed his heart and eyes to look at the allurements of the world and the deception of Satan. Her strong opinions and domineering attitude only added to the problem. Sparing the details, they lost the bliss they once enjoyed. It was a miserable existence for both of them. He was neither repentant nor asking forgiveness, but she continually forgave and pointed the children (five by now) to “we hate the sin, but we love our daddy.” After many years of broken oneness, her commitment to “whither thou goest, I will go” began a miracle. God’s grace was sufficient.

Why are they so happy now?

First, it must be said, it was the power of God working in both of their lives. God didn’t give up on them. He said He wouldn’t; and He didn’t. They were tempted but they didn’t go where Satan wanted them to go. They both have experienced the power of the Holy Spirit to bring them to depths of spiritual communion that they never knew before. It took many heart-wrenching prayers for strength and forgiveness. It took many deep, heartfelt tears of repentance and close accountability to each other. Many and much!

Secondly, as they look back to that time in their lives, there were four principles of God’s Word that were engrained so deeply into their minds that they couldn’t deny them:

  1. A covenant with God is powerful and cannot be broken.
  2. Unconditional love for another person is powerful.
  3. Real and ongoing personal repentance is powerful.
  4. Living a life (moment by moment) of forgiveness is powerful.

When those four God-ordained choices enter a war between the will of God and the wiles of the enemy, the enemy is powerless.

A covenant with God is undeniably unbreakable. When “the books are opened” the covenant will not have changed.

Unconditional love means loving even when it’s not so easy. Fires have a tendency to go out when they have cold water thrown on them. It requires a lot of staying really close to Jesus! Ann’s prayer and plea to God was “Lord, please draw Mark back to You by the power of Your Holy Spirit.” God answered!

When I, Mark, realized what I was losing, both in eternity and in this life with my family, and the depth and sinfulness of my sin, I trembled before God. He brought me to repentance. God began a healing that was exceeding and abundantly above all that Ann and I had ever thought or asked. My deep, heart-wrenching, grief-stricken repentance was real and obvious to her and the family. I took 100% of the blame. Everyone knows “there are always two sides to the story,” yet as the one who had committed the sin, I took full responsibility for my sin and the chaos that was brought into the marriage. I never blamed her for my sin. Humility is not difficult when it is heartfelt and Holy Spirit-guided!

My, Ann’s response to Mark’s repentance was full and free forgiveness. His ongoing expression of repentance and the fact that he took all the blame was powerful in rebuilding trust. It was clear that God was blessing our marriage again! The sun was shining through clouds that were rapidly receding!

Today, 23 years later, photos of that season in our lives or some reminiscent moment is apt to wash up fresh tears of grief and repentance for the pain and wasted years. Ongoing repentance and ready forgiveness have proven beautiful in building trust and a relationship that is sweeter and stronger than ever before! God truly has fulfilled His promise to … restore to [us] the years that the locust hath eaten! (Joel 2:25a) Praise the Lord!

For nesten 43 år siden, en varm augustettermiddag, kom to 19-åringer (en ung kvinne og forloveden hennes) begeistret ut av foreldrenes hjem og gikk langsomt ned en liten bakke mot en gruppe på 200 mennesker som ventet. Faren hennes, en predikant, ventet på dem foran midtgangen. Røde av begeistring sto de foran ham og lyttet til den korte talen han hadde forberedt om ekteskapet. Med hjertene bankende av forventning svarte de glad «Ja», og inngikk en pakt med hverandre og med Gud.

De forsto begge hva det betydde å være trofaste «i sykdom og helse, i fattigdom og rikdom, i gode og onde dager, til døden skiller oss». Generasjoner før dem hadde vist dem at det var mulig. Foreldre og søsken hadde vist dem det. Onkler og tanter hadde vist dem det. Dette skulle bli en lykke som varte til livets høst … trodde de i hvert fall.

Det falt dem aldri inn at store prøvelser skulle sette selve kjernen i troen og forpliktelsen deres på prøve. De gikk gjennom vanskelige økonomiske tider. (Saldoen i sjekkheftet var lavere enn regningene som skulle betales.) De sto overfor livsforandrende beslutninger. (Han ville slutte i jobben hos svigerfaren, der han bygde skap og fikk fast lønn, og begynne å drive gård sammen med faren sin, noe som ikke garanterte noen inntekt hver uke, langt mindre hvert år. Hun var ikke så sikker.) På dette tidspunktet hadde de fire barn og kjente utfordringen med gråtende babyer og søvnløse netter, som gjorde alle utslitte. De kjente til meningsforskjellene som fra tid til annen oppsto på menighetsmøtene, og som fikk dem til å lure på hva de skulle mene. (En bror mente én ting, en annen mente noe annet, men dette paret respekterte begge brødrene.) Tolv års erfaringer lå bak dem; likevel var ekteskapet lykkelig og godt. Livets sol skinte klart!

Så skjedde det … Skyene begynte å rulle inn i tette, mørke bølger! Åtte år med elendighet og et dysfunksjonelt forhold lå foran dem. Djevelen arbeidet hardt for å ødelegge samholdet og gleden hos disse to, som hadde et så vakkert ekteskap. Han lot hjertet og blikket sitt bli dratt mot verdens fristelser og Satans bedrag. Hennes sterke meninger og dominerende holdning gjorde bare problemet større. For å spare dere for detaljene mistet de lykken de en gang hadde hatt. Tilværelsen var elendig for dem begge. Han angret ikke og ba heller ikke om tilgivelse, men hun tilga ham stadig og viste barna (nå fem) at «vi hater synden, men elsker pappaen vår». Etter mange år med brutt enhet ble hennes forpliktelse til «dit du går, vil jeg gå» begynnelsen på et mirakel. Guds nåde var nok.

Hvorfor er de så lykkelige nå?

Først må det sies at det var Guds kraft som virket i begges liv. Gud ga dem ikke opp. Han sa at han ikke ville gjøre det, og det gjorde han heller ikke. De ble fristet, men gikk ikke dit Satan ville føre dem. Begge har erfart Den hellige ånds kraft, som har ført dem til dybder av åndelig fellesskap de aldri før hadde kjent. Det krevde mange hjerteskjærende bønner om styrke og tilgivelse. Det krevde mange dype, inderlige tårer i omvendelse og at de holdt hverandre tett ansvarlige. Mye og mange!

For det andre: Når de ser tilbake på den tiden i livet, var det fire prinsipper fra Guds Ord som var så dypt inngravert i sinnet deres at de ikke kunne benekte dem:

  1. En pakt med Gud er mektig og kan ikke brytes.
  2. Ubetinget kjærlighet til et annet menneske er mektig.
  3. Ekte og vedvarende personlig omvendelse er mektig.
  4. Å leve et liv (øyeblikk for øyeblikk) i tilgivelse er mektig.

Når disse fire valgene, som Gud har bestemt, går inn i en kamp mellom Guds vilje og fiendens list, er fienden maktesløs.

En pakt med Gud kan utvilsomt ikke brytes. Når «bøkene åpnes», vil pakten ikke ha forandret seg.

Ubetinget kjærlighet betyr å elske også når det ikke er så lett. Ild har en tendens til å slukne når den blir kastet kaldt vann på. Det krever at man holder seg svært nær Jesus! Anns bønn og inderlige bønn til Gud var: «Herre, vær så snill å føre Mark tilbake til deg ved Den hellige ånds kraft.» Gud svarte!

Da jeg, Mark, innså hva jeg var i ferd med å miste, både i evigheten og her i livet sammen med familien min, og hvor dypt syndig synden min var, skalv jeg for Gud. Han førte meg til omvendelse. Gud begynte en helbredelse som gikk langt ut over alt Ann og jeg noen gang hadde tenkt eller bedt om. Min dype, hjerteskjærende og sorgfylte omvendelse var ekte og tydelig for henne og familien. Jeg tok 100 % av skylden. Alle vet at «det finnes alltid to sider av saken», men som den som hadde begått synden, tok jeg fullt ansvar for synden min og kaoset jeg hadde brakt inn i ekteskapet. Jeg skyldte aldri på henne for synden min. Ydmykhet er ikke vanskelig når den er oppriktig og ledet av Den hellige ånd!

Min, Anns, reaksjon på Marks omvendelse var full og fri tilgivelse. Hans vedvarende uttrykk for omvendelse og det at han tok all skylden, var avgjørende for å bygge opp tilliten igjen. Det var tydelig at Gud velsignet ekteskapet vårt på nytt! Solen skinte gjennom skyene som raskt trakk seg tilbake!

I dag, 23 år senere, kan bilder fra den tiden i livet vårt eller et minne vekke friske tårer av sorg og omvendelse over smerten og de bortkastede årene. Vedvarende omvendelse og villig tilgivelse har vist seg å være vakkert i arbeidet med å bygge opp tillit og et forhold som er mer nært og sterkere enn noen gang før! Gud har virkelig oppfylt sitt løfte om å … gi [oss] igjen de år som gresshoppen har fortært! (Joel 2:25a) Lovet være Herren!

Nearly 43 years ago, on a warm August afternoon, two 19-year-olds (a young woman and her fiancé) excitedly came out of her parents’ home and walked slowly down a small hill toward a group of 200 waiting people. Her father, a minister, awaited them at the front of the aisle. Flushed with excitement they stood before him and listened to the short message he had prepared concerning marriage. Their hearts beating with anticipation they joyfully answered, “I do,” making a covenant with each other and with God.

They both understood what it meant to remain faithful “through sickness and health, poverty and wealth, for better or worse, till death do us part.” Generations before had shown them that it was possible. Parents and siblings had shown them. Uncles and aunts had shown them. This was going to be bliss into life’s sunset… Or so they thought.

It never entered their minds that great trials would test the very core of their belief and commitment. They went through hard financial times. (The balance in the checkbook was less than the bills that were due.) They went through times of life-changing decisions. (He wanted to quit his job working for his father-in-law building cabinets, receiving a regular paycheck, and begin farming with his father, which didn’t guarantee any income each week, let alone each year. She wasn’t so sure.) They had four children by this time and knew the challenge of crying babies and sleepless nights, which left everyone exhausted. They knew the differences that came up from time to time in church meetings that left them wondering which way they should think. (One brother thought one way and another thought differently, yet this couple respected both brothers.) Twelve years of experiences were behind them; still, married life was blissful and happy. Life’s sun was shining brightly!

Then it happened… The clouds began to roll in thick, angry waves! Eight years of misery and dysfunction were ahead. The devil was hard at work to destroy the unity and joy of these two whose marriage was going so beautifully. He allowed his heart and eyes to look at the allurements of the world and the deception of Satan. Her strong opinions and domineering attitude only added to the problem. Sparing the details, they lost the bliss they once enjoyed. It was a miserable existence for both of them. He was neither repentant nor asking forgiveness, but she continually forgave and pointed the children (five by now) to “we hate the sin, but we love our daddy.” After many years of broken oneness, her commitment to “whither thou goest, I will go” began a miracle. God’s grace was sufficient.

Why are they so happy now?

First, it must be said, it was the power of God working in both of their lives. God didn’t give up on them. He said He wouldn’t; and He didn’t. They were tempted but they didn’t go where Satan wanted them to go. They both have experienced the power of the Holy Spirit to bring them to depths of spiritual communion that they never knew before. It took many heart-wrenching prayers for strength and forgiveness. It took many deep, heartfelt tears of repentance and close accountability to each other. Many and much!

Secondly, as they look back to that time in their lives, there were four principles of God’s Word that were engrained so deeply into their minds that they couldn’t deny them:

  1. A covenant with God is powerful and cannot be broken.
  2. Unconditional love for another person is powerful.
  3. Real and ongoing personal repentance is powerful.
  4. Living a life (moment by moment) of forgiveness is powerful.

When those four God-ordained choices enter a war between the will of God and the wiles of the enemy, the enemy is powerless.

A covenant with God is undeniably unbreakable. When “the books are opened” the covenant will not have changed.

Unconditional love means loving even when it’s not so easy. Fires have a tendency to go out when they have cold water thrown on them. It requires a lot of staying really close to Jesus! Ann’s prayer and plea to God was “Lord, please draw Mark back to You by the power of Your Holy Spirit.” God answered!

When I, Mark, realized what I was losing, both in eternity and in this life with my family, and the depth and sinfulness of my sin, I trembled before God. He brought me to repentance. God began a healing that was exceeding and abundantly above all that Ann and I had ever thought or asked. My deep, heart-wrenching, grief-stricken repentance was real and obvious to her and the family. I took 100% of the blame. Everyone knows “there are always two sides to the story,” yet as the one who had committed the sin, I took full responsibility for my sin and the chaos that was brought into the marriage. I never blamed her for my sin. Humility is not difficult when it is heartfelt and Holy Spirit-guided!

My, Ann’s response to Mark’s repentance was full and free forgiveness. His ongoing expression of repentance and the fact that he took all the blame was powerful in rebuilding trust. It was clear that God was blessing our marriage again! The sun was shining through clouds that were rapidly receding!

Today, 23 years later, photos of that season in our lives or some reminiscent moment is apt to wash up fresh tears of grief and repentance for the pain and wasted years. Ongoing repentance and ready forgiveness have proven beautiful in building trust and a relationship that is sweeter and stronger than ever before! God truly has fulfilled His promise to … restore to [us] the years that the locust hath eaten! (Joel 2:25a) Praise the Lord!

거의 43년 전, 따뜻한 8월 어느 오후, 열아홉 살인 두 사람(젊은 여성과 그녀의 약혼자)은 들뜬 마음으로 부모님 집을 나와 기다리고 있던 200명의 사람들을 향해 작은 언덕길을 천천히 걸어 내려갔습니다. 목사인 그녀의 아버지는 통로 앞쪽에서 그들을 기다리고 있었습니다. 두 사람은 설렘에 얼굴이 상기된 채 아버지 앞에 서서, 아버지가 결혼에 관해 준비한 짧은 메시지를 들었습니다. 기대감에 가슴이 뛰는 가운데 두 사람은 기쁘게 “그러겠습니다”라고 대답하며 서로와 하나님 앞에서 언약을 맺었습니다.

두 사람은 “아플 때나 건강할 때나, 가난할 때나 부유할 때나, 좋을 때나 나쁠 때나, 죽음이 우리를 갈라놓을 때까지” 서로에게 충실하다는 것이 무엇을 뜻하는지 잘 알고 있었습니다. 그보다 앞선 세대들이 그것이 가능하다는 것을 보여 주었습니다. 부모와 형제자매들이 보여 주었습니다. 삼촌과 이모, 고모들이 보여 주었습니다. 인생의 황혼까지 행복하리라… 적어도 그들은 그렇게 생각했습니다.

큰 시련이 자신들의 믿음과 헌신의 핵심을 시험하리라고는 전혀 생각하지 못했습니다. 두 사람은 힘든 경제적 시기를 겪었습니다. (수표책의 잔고가 납부해야 할 청구 금액보다 적었습니다.) 인생을 바꾸는 결정을 내려야 하는 때도 겪었습니다. (그는 장인 밑에서 정기적으로 급여를 받으며 가구를 만드는 일을 그만두고 아버지와 농사를 시작하고 싶어 했습니다. 농사일은 매주, 심지어 매년이라도 수입이 보장되지 않았습니다. 그녀는 확신이 서지 않았습니다.) 그 무렵 두 사람에게는 아이가 넷 있었고, 울어 대는 아기들과 잠 못 이루는 밤이 모두를 지치게 하는 어려움도 알고 있었습니다. 교회 모임에서 이따금 의견 차이가 생겨 어느 쪽으로 생각해야 할지 고민하기도 했습니다. (한 형제는 한쪽 의견을, 다른 형제는 다른 의견을 가졌지만, 이 부부는 두 형제를 모두 존중했습니다.) 12년간의 경험이 쌓여 있었고, 그래도 결혼 생활은 행복하고 즐거웠습니다. 인생의 태양은 환하게 빛나고 있었습니다!

그러다 일이 벌어졌습니다… 먹구름이 짙고 사나운 파도처럼 밀려오기 시작했습니다! 앞으로 8년간 불행과 파탄의 시간이 기다리고 있었습니다. 마귀는 아름답게 이어지던 이 두 사람의 결혼 생활에서 화합과 기쁨을 무너뜨리려고 열심히 일했습니다. 그는 세상의 유혹과 사탄의 속임수에 마음과 눈을 돌리도록 내버려 두었습니다. 그녀의 강한 주장과 지배적인 태도는 문제를 더 악화시켰습니다. 자세한 이야기는 생략하자면, 두 사람은 한때 누렸던 행복을 잃었습니다. 둘 다 비참한 삶을 살았습니다. 그는 회개하지도 않았고 용서를 구하지도 않았지만, 그녀는 계속해서 용서했고 아이들(그때는 다섯이었습니다)에게 “우리는 죄는 미워하지만 아빠는 사랑해”라고 가르쳤습니다. 오랫동안 하나 됨이 깨진 채 지낸 끝에, “당신이 가는 곳에 나도 가겠습니다”라는 그녀의 헌신이 기적의 시작이 되었습니다. 하나님의 은혜는 충분했습니다.

그들은 이제 왜 그렇게 행복할까요?

먼저 말해야 할 것은, 두 사람의 삶 속에서 역사하신 하나님의 능력이었다는 점입니다. 하나님께서는 그들을 포기하지 않으셨습니다. 포기하지 않겠다고 말씀하셨고, 실제로 포기하지 않으셨습니다. 두 사람은 유혹을 받았지만 사탄이 이끌고자 한 곳으로 가지 않았습니다. 두 사람 모두 성령의 능력을 경험하며, 이전에는 알지 못했던 깊은 영적 교제에 이르게 되었습니다. 힘과 용서를 구하는 마음을 찢는 기도를 수없이 드려야 했습니다. 진심 어린 깊은 회개의 눈물과 서로에 대한 긴밀한 책임 의식도 필요했습니다. 참으로 많은 것을, 많이도 겪었습니다!

둘째로, 두 사람이 그 시절을 되돌아보면, 하나님의 말씀에 담긴 네 가지 원리가 마음에 너무 깊이 새겨져 있어 부인할 수 없었습니다.

  1. 하나님과 맺은 언약에는 능력이 있으며 깨뜨릴 수 없습니다.
  2. 다른 사람을 향한 무조건적인 사랑에는 능력이 있습니다.
  3. 진실하고 지속적인 개인의 회개에는 능력이 있습니다.
  4. 순간순간 용서하며 사는 삶에는 능력이 있습니다.

하나님께서 정하신 이 네 가지 선택이 하나님의 뜻과 원수의 간계가 맞서는 싸움에 들어서면, 원수는 무력해집니다.

하나님과 맺은 언약은 분명히 깨뜨릴 수 없습니다. “책들이 펼쳐질” 때에도 그 언약은 달라져 있지 않을 것입니다.

무조건적인 사랑은 쉽지 않을 때에도 사랑하는 것을 뜻합니다. 불 위에 찬물을 끼얹으면 불이 꺼지기 쉽습니다. 예수님께 아주 가까이 머무는 일이 많이 필요합니다! 앤은 “주님, 성령의 능력으로 마크를 주님께로 다시 이끌어 주소서”라고 하나님께 기도하며 간구했습니다. 하나님께서 응답하셨습니다!

가족과 함께 누리는 이 삶과 영원한 삶에서 내가 무엇을 잃고 있는지, 또 내 죄가 얼마나 깊고 악한지 깨달았을 때, 나는 마크로서 하나님 앞에서 떨었습니다. 하나님께서는 나를 회개하게 하셨습니다. 하나님께서는 앤과 내가 생각하거나 구했던 것보다도 훨씬 더 넘치도록 치유를 시작하셨습니다. 내 마음을 찢고 깊은 슬픔을 동반한 회개는 진실했으며, 아내와 가족에게 분명히 드러났습니다. 나는 책임을 100퍼센트 짊어졌습니다. 모두가 “이야기에는 늘 양쪽의 입장이 있다”는 것을 알지만, 죄를 저지른 사람으로서 나는 내 죄와 그 죄가 결혼 생활에 가져온 혼란에 대해 전적으로 책임을 졌습니다. 내 죄를 그녀 탓으로 돌린 적은 한 번도 없습니다. 마음에서 우러나고 성령의 인도를 받는 겸손은 어렵지 않습니다!

마크의 회개에 대한 나, 앤의 반응은 온전하고 아낌없는 용서였습니다. 그가 계속 회개를 표현하고 모든 책임을 자신이 졌다는 사실은 신뢰를 회복하는 데 큰 힘이 되었습니다. 하나님께서 우리 결혼 생활에 다시 복을 주고 계신 것이 분명했습니다! 구름이 빠르게 걷히며 햇살이 비치고 있었습니다!

오늘, 23년이 지난 지금도 그 시절의 사진이나 그때를 떠올리게 하는 순간을 마주하면, 고통과 허비한 세월을 생각하며 슬픔과 회개의 눈물이 새롭게 솟아오르곤 합니다. 지속적인 회개와 기꺼운 용서는 신뢰를 쌓고 그 어느 때보다 더 달콤하고 강한 관계를 이루는 데 아름다운 열매를 맺었습니다! 하나님께서는 참으로 그분의 약속을 이루셨습니다… 메뚜기가 먹은 [우리의] 햇수를 회복하여 주셨습니다! (요엘 2:25a) 주님을 찬양합니다!

Nearly 43 years ago, on a warm August afternoon, two 19-year-olds (a young woman and her fiancé) excitedly came out of her parents’ home and walked slowly down a small hill toward a group of 200 waiting people. Her father, a minister, awaited them at the front of the aisle. Flushed with excitement they stood before him and listened to the short message he had prepared concerning marriage. Their hearts beating with anticipation they joyfully answered, “I do,” making a covenant with each other and with God.

They both understood what it meant to remain faithful “through sickness and health, poverty and wealth, for better or worse, till death do us part.” Generations before had shown them that it was possible. Parents and siblings had shown them. Uncles and aunts had shown them. This was going to be bliss into life’s sunset… Or so they thought.

It never entered their minds that great trials would test the very core of their belief and commitment. They went through hard financial times. (The balance in the checkbook was less than the bills that were due.) They went through times of life-changing decisions. (He wanted to quit his job working for his father-in-law building cabinets, receiving a regular paycheck, and begin farming with his father, which didn’t guarantee any income each week, let alone each year. She wasn’t so sure.) They had four children by this time and knew the challenge of crying babies and sleepless nights, which left everyone exhausted. They knew the differences that came up from time to time in church meetings that left them wondering which way they should think. (One brother thought one way and another thought differently, yet this couple respected both brothers.) Twelve years of experiences were behind them; still, married life was blissful and happy. Life’s sun was shining brightly!

Then it happened… The clouds began to roll in thick, angry waves! Eight years of misery and dysfunction were ahead. The devil was hard at work to destroy the unity and joy of these two whose marriage was going so beautifully. He allowed his heart and eyes to look at the allurements of the world and the deception of Satan. Her strong opinions and domineering attitude only added to the problem. Sparing the details, they lost the bliss they once enjoyed. It was a miserable existence for both of them. He was neither repentant nor asking forgiveness, but she continually forgave and pointed the children (five by now) to “we hate the sin, but we love our daddy.” After many years of broken oneness, her commitment to “whither thou goest, I will go” began a miracle. God’s grace was sufficient.

Why are they so happy now?

First, it must be said, it was the power of God working in both of their lives. God didn’t give up on them. He said He wouldn’t; and He didn’t. They were tempted but they didn’t go where Satan wanted them to go. They both have experienced the power of the Holy Spirit to bring them to depths of spiritual communion that they never knew before. It took many heart-wrenching prayers for strength and forgiveness. It took many deep, heartfelt tears of repentance and close accountability to each other. Many and much!

Secondly, as they look back to that time in their lives, there were four principles of God’s Word that were engrained so deeply into their minds that they couldn’t deny them:

  1. A covenant with God is powerful and cannot be broken.
  2. Unconditional love for another person is powerful.
  3. Real and ongoing personal repentance is powerful.
  4. Living a life (moment by moment) of forgiveness is powerful.

When those four God-ordained choices enter a war between the will of God and the wiles of the enemy, the enemy is powerless.

A covenant with God is undeniably unbreakable. When “the books are opened” the covenant will not have changed.

Unconditional love means loving even when it’s not so easy. Fires have a tendency to go out when they have cold water thrown on them. It requires a lot of staying really close to Jesus! Ann’s prayer and plea to God was “Lord, please draw Mark back to You by the power of Your Holy Spirit.” God answered!

When I, Mark, realized what I was losing, both in eternity and in this life with my family, and the depth and sinfulness of my sin, I trembled before God. He brought me to repentance. God began a healing that was exceeding and abundantly above all that Ann and I had ever thought or asked. My deep, heart-wrenching, grief-stricken repentance was real and obvious to her and the family. I took 100% of the blame. Everyone knows “there are always two sides to the story,” yet as the one who had committed the sin, I took full responsibility for my sin and the chaos that was brought into the marriage. I never blamed her for my sin. Humility is not difficult when it is heartfelt and Holy Spirit-guided!

My, Ann’s response to Mark’s repentance was full and free forgiveness. His ongoing expression of repentance and the fact that he took all the blame was powerful in rebuilding trust. It was clear that God was blessing our marriage again! The sun was shining through clouds that were rapidly receding!

Today, 23 years later, photos of that season in our lives or some reminiscent moment is apt to wash up fresh tears of grief and repentance for the pain and wasted years. Ongoing repentance and ready forgiveness have proven beautiful in building trust and a relationship that is sweeter and stronger than ever before! God truly has fulfilled His promise to … restore to [us] the years that the locust hath eaten! (Joel 2:25a) Praise the Lord!

Amper 43 jaar gelede, op ’n warm Augustusmiddag, het twee 19-jariges (’n jong vrou en haar verloofde) opgewonde uit haar ouers se huis gekom en stadig teen ’n klein heuwel af gestap na ’n groep van 200 mense wat gewag het. Haar pa, ’n predikant, het hulle voor in die paadjie ingewag. Met opgewondenheid wat op hulle gesigte te sien was, het hulle voor hom gaan staan en geluister na die kort boodskap oor die huwelik wat hy voorberei het. Met harte wat van afwagting geklop het, het hulle met vreugde geantwoord: “Ja,” en so ’n verbond met mekaar en met God gesluit.

Hulle het albei verstaan wat dit beteken om getrou te bly “in siekte en gesondheid, in armoede en rykdom, ten goede of ten kwade, totdat die dood ons skei.” Geslagte voor hulle het gewys dat dit moontlik was. Ouers en broers en susters het dit vir hulle gewys. Ooms en tantes het dit vir hulle gewys. Dit sou ’n salige lewe wees tot teen sononder… Of so het hulle gedink.

Dit het nooit by hulle opgekom dat groot beproewings die kern van hulle geloof en toewyding sou toets nie. Hulle het moeilike tye finansieel beleef. (Die saldo in die tjekboek was minder as die rekeninge wat betaal moes word.) Hulle het tye beleef waarin hulle lewensveranderende besluite moes neem. (Hy wou ophou met sy werk om kaste vir sy skoonpa te bou, waarvoor hy ’n gereelde salaris ontvang het, en saam met sy pa begin boer—’n onderneming wat geen inkomste elke week, wat nog te sê elke jaar, gewaarborg het nie. Sy was nie so seker nie.) Teen daardie tyd het hulle vier kinders gehad en het hulle geweet hoe veeleisend huilende babas en slapelose nagte is, wat almal uitgeput gelaat het. Hulle het geweet van meningsverskille wat van tyd tot tyd in kerkvergaderings ontstaan het en hulle laat wonder het hoe hulle moes dink. (Een broer het een siening gehad en ’n ander broer het anders gedink, maar hierdie egpaar het albei broers gerespekteer.) Twaalf jaar se ondervindinge was agter die rug; tog was die getroude lewe salig en gelukkig. Die son van die lewe het helder geskyn!

Toe gebeur dit… Die wolke het in digte, dreigende golwe begin opkom! Agt jaar van ellende en wanfunksionering het voorgelê. Die duiwel was hard aan die werk om die eenheid en vreugde van hierdie twee, wie se huwelik so mooi verloop het, te vernietig. Hy het toegelaat dat sy hart en oë aangetrek word deur die verleidinge van die wêreld en Satan se misleiding. Haar sterk menings en baasspelerige houding het die probleem net vererger. Om die besonderhede oor te slaan: hulle het die saligheid verloor wat hulle eens geniet het. Vir hulle albei was dit ’n ellendige bestaan. Hy was nie berouvol nie en het ook nie om vergifnis gevra nie, maar sy het hom aanhoudend vergewe en die kinders (teen daardie tyd vyf) daarop gewys: “ons haat die sonde, maar ons is lief vir ons pa.” Ná baie jare van gebroke eenheid het haar toewyding aan “waarheen jy gaan, sal ek gaan” ’n wonderwerk begin. God se genade was genoeg.

Waarom is hulle nou so gelukkig?

Eerstens moet gesê word dat dit die krag van God was wat in albei se lewens gewerk het. God het hulle nie opgegee nie. Hy het gesê Hy sou dit nie doen nie; en Hy het dit nie gedoen nie. Hulle is versoek, maar hulle het nie gegaan waar Satan wou hê hulle moes gaan nie. Hulle het albei die krag van die Heilige Gees ervaar om hulle tot dieptes van geestelike gemeenskap te bring wat hulle voorheen nooit geken het nie. Dit het baie hartverskeurende gebede om krag en vergifnis gekos. Dit het baie diep, opregte trane van bekering en wedersydse, noukeurige aanspreeklikheid gekos. Baie en nog baie meer!

Tweedens, wanneer hulle terugkyk op daardie tyd in hulle lewens, was daar vier beginsels uit God se Woord wat so diep in hulle gedagtes ingeprent was dat hulle dit nie kon ontken nie:

  1. ’n Verbond met God is kragtig en kan nie verbreek word nie.
  2. Onvoorwaardelike liefde vir ’n ander persoon is kragtig.
  3. Ware en volgehoue persoonlike bekering is kragtig.
  4. Om (oomblik vir oomblik) ’n lewe van vergifnis te lei, is kragtig.

Wanneer daardie vier keuses, wat deur God verorden is, in ’n stryd tussen die wil van God en die vyand se listigheid betrokke raak, is die vyand magteloos.

’n Verbond met God is onbetwisbaar onbreekbaar. Wanneer “die boeke geopen word”, sal die verbond nie verander het nie.

Onvoorwaardelike liefde beteken dat jy liefhet selfs wanneer dit nie so maklik is nie. Vure het die neiging om dood te gaan wanneer koue water daarop gegooi word. Dit verg dat jy baie na aan Jesus bly! Ann se gebed en pleidooi tot God was: “Here, trek Mark asseblief deur die krag van u Heilige Gees terug na U.” God het geantwoord!

Toe ek, Mark, besef wat ek besig was om te verloor, sowel in die ewigheid as in hierdie lewe saam met my gesin, en hoe diep en sondig my sonde was, het ek voor God gebewe. Hy het my tot bekering gebring. God het ’n genesing begin wat veel meer was as alles wat Ann en ek ooit kon dink of vra. My diepe, hartverskeurende en droewige bekering was werklik en duidelik vir haar en die gesin. Ek het 100% van die skuld aanvaar. Almal weet “daar is altyd twee kante aan die saak,” maar as die een wat die sonde begaan het, het ek volle verantwoordelikheid vir my sonde en die chaos wat dit in die huwelik gebring het, aanvaar. Ek het haar nooit vir my sonde blameer nie. Nederigheid is nie moeilik wanneer dit uit die hart kom en deur die Heilige Gees gelei word nie!

My, Ann, se reaksie op Mark se bekering was om hom volledig en vryelik te vergewe. Sy volgehoue uiting van berou en die feit dat hy al die skuld aanvaar het, was kragtig om vertroue te herbou. Dit was duidelik dat God ons huwelik weer geseën het! Die son het deur wolke geskyn wat vinnig besig was om weg te trek!

Vandag, 23 jaar later, bring foto’s van daardie tyd in ons lewens, of ’n herinnering daaraan, maklik vars trane van droefheid en bekering oor die pyn en vermorste jare. Voortdurende bekering en gewillige vergifnis het bewys hoe mooi dit is om vertroue en ’n verhouding op te bou wat soeter en sterker as ooit tevore is! God het inderdaad sy belofte vervul om … die jare wat die sprinkaan [van ons] geëet het, aan [ons] terug te gee! (Joël 2:25a) Loof die Here!
